title: Toronto police officer cleared in shooting death of knife-wielding man
subtitle: The Special Investigations Unit has concluded there are no reasonable grounds to charge a Toronto police officer in relation to a shooting death.
article: The province's police watchdog has concluded there are no reasonable grounds to charge a Toronto police officer in the shooting death of a 39-year-old man in Scarborough last month.
Police were called to an apartment on Adanac Dr., near Eglinton Ave. E. and Markham Rd., for a disturbance involving a man who was armed with a knife at about 6 p.m. on June 8.

The Special Investigations Unit said the officer in question and her partner entered the apartment's second floor and opened the door to the stairwell where they heard Malcolm Jackman talking to himself. A short confrontation revealed he was armed with a knife

After a shouting match and a failed attempt to subdue him with pepper spray, Jackman ran out of the building and when the officers caught up with him, they saw he was holding a person hostage at knifepoint, the SIU said in a news release Tuesday.
The officers asked Jackman to drop the knife multiple times but shot at him once they noticed the knife moving closer to his hostage's neck, the SIU said.

"In my view, the subject officer's use of lethal force was justified in these circumstances," said Ian Scott, director of the SIU. "Mr. Jackman represented an imminent threat of death or serious bodily harm to the citizen. Accordingly, I am of the view that she had no reasonable choice but to discharge her firearm to stop this imminent threat to the person who the decedent had taken hostage."
The SIU is an arm's length agency that investigates reports involving police where there has been death, serious injury or allegations of sexual assault.
